findings.summary: VPC peering is claimed to support overlapping CIDR blocks, which AWS categorically forbids.
findings.evidence: "Supports overlapping CIDR with caution" (section "4. VPC Peering")
findings.fix: Replace with "VPCs must have non-overlapping CIDR blocks — a peering request between matching/overlapping CIDRs goes straight to failed"; suggest Transit Gateway + NAT or re-IP when ranges collide.

findings.summary: A leftover networking section is wedged into the middle of the storage chapter, splitting the S3 section's bullets from its diagram.
findings.evidence: Page 8 ends with "2. S3" and its bullets ("Object storage, highly durable (11 9s)"); page 9 then opens with "10. NACL vs SG" and the table ["Type","Stateless","Stateful"], and only after it comes the S3 diagram {"nodes":["S3 Bucket","Image","Doc","Video"]} followed by "3. EFS".
findings.fix: Move the "10. NACL vs SG" heading and table back to the end of the networking chapter (before the "A variety of storage and file services" intro paragraph on page 8), so the S3 bullets and the S3 Bucket diagram stay adjacent and storage runs 1→2→3 uninterrupted.

findings.summary: The handbook ends on an orphan chapter-intro paragraph whose chapter, and the four chapters after it, are never delivered.
findings.evidence: Final block of the final page: {"type":"paragraph","text":"Management and monitoring services to ==operate resources efficiently==."} — no CloudWatch, CloudTrail, Config, SSM, CloudFormation, Trusted Advisor, EventBridge or Organizations sections follow, and syllabus chapters 12–16 (Database Deep Dive, Compute Services, Networking Services, Storage Services) are absent entirely.
findings.fix: Either add the Management & Monitoring sections (and the remaining syllabus chapters) after this paragraph, or delete the dangling intro paragraph so the handbook closes on a completed section.

findings.summary: The sample IAM policy pairs s3:ListBucket with an object-level ARN, so the policy grants nothing.
findings.evidence: "\"Action\": [\"s3:ListBucket\"]," with "\"Resource\": [\"arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*\"]"
findings.fix: Use the bucket ARN for bucket-level actions: "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket"] (keep the /* form only for object actions such as s3:GetObject), matching the correct example on page 10.

findings.summary: The "How IAM Works" diagram renders the two mutually exclusive outcomes as consecutive steps in a single chain.
findings.evidence: {"nodes":["User/Role","Requests AWS","IAM checks policy",{"text":"Access Allowed"},{"text":"Access Denied"}]} — a learner reads "Access Allowed -> Access Denied" as a sequence.
findings.fix: Render the last step as a branch off "IAM checks policy" (or label the two nodes "if Allow" / "if Deny") so they read as alternatives, not successive stages.

findings.summary: A single route table is shown with two conflicting 0.0.0.0/0 routes, which AWS rejects since one destination CIDR can have only one target.
findings.evidence: Table "5. Route Table" rows "["0.0.0.0/0","Internet Gateway"]" and "["0.0.0.0/0","NAT Gateway"]"
findings.fix: Split into two labelled tables — public route table (local + 0.0.0.0/0 → IGW) and private route table (local + 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT GW).

findings.summary: The VPN connection flow chain wraps mid-diagram, leaving an arrow pointing into empty space at the end of the first row.
findings.evidence: Row reads "On-Premises → VPN Tunnel (IPSec) →" with nothing after the final arrow; the next node "VPC 10.0.0.0/16" is rendered on the line below, starting back at the left margin.
findings.fix: Let the flow chain wrap as a unit — suppress the trailing connector when a row ends, or shrink node padding/font for this chain so "On-Premises → VPN Tunnel (IPSec) → VPC 10.0.0.0/16" fits on one row.

findings.summary: EFS is said to use NFS v4.2, a version Amazon EFS does not support.
findings.evidence: "Uses NFS (v4.1 and v4.2)" (section "3. EFS")
findings.fix: Change to "Uses NFS (v4.0 and v4.1; v4.1 recommended)" — EFS supports no NFSv2/v3 and no v4.2.

findings.summary: The storage-class table understates availability for the two deep archive classes, which AWS designs for 99.99%, not 99.9%.
findings.evidence: Rows "["Glacier Flexible","Archive minutes-hours","99.9%"]" and "["Glacier Deep Archive","Long term lowest cost","99.9%"]"
findings.fix: Set both Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Glacier Deep Archive availability to 99.99% (Glacier Instant Retrieval stays 99.9%).

findings.summary: The encryption options flow chain wraps so the second row begins with an orphaned arrow that has no source node.
findings.evidence: First row is "Data at Rest (EBS, S3, RDS) → Data in Transit (SSL/TLS)"; the next line starts with a bare "→" before "Key Management (KMS)".
findings.fix: Apply the same chain-wrap handling as page 8: drop the leading connector on a wrapped row (or reflow the three nodes into one row) so no arrow is left without a node on one side.
